correctness.rationale: Rearrangement and a single forced sign mismatch give matching upper and lower bounds on D-orbit support. Adding antipodal support losses handles both parity cases, and the unit-sphere minimum coordinate gives exact Hausdorff distance. Half-normal minimum extreme-value convergence and independent Gaussian sign parity imply both distribution limits; inverse-chi moments and exponential-minimum tails justify moments. Direct small-rank orbit enumeration independently reproduces the identities in 27 deterministic cases.

originality.rationale: Compared exact statements and implications with a full open-access article on type-B permutohedra, indexed Coxeter deformation geometry, published published-finding corpus records and accessible own-claim history. The identified theorem concerns a paired B/D support defect, exact Hausdorff modulus, parity-zero atom, and universal exponential law absent from the closest inspected source statements. Generic orbit maximization does not itself state the coupled distribution, but equivalent less-indexed derivations remain possible.
residual_risks: Part of the original Coxeter deformation paper could not be inspected as a complete document; its accessible sections indicate a distinct problem but cannot certify a whole-document negative.

Generic Weyl orbit convex-hull theory may make the elementary finite support identity readily derivable; originality attaches to the combined exact gap and parity-dependent probability law, not to the rearrangement principle itself.

value.rationale: The paired Coxeter orbits lose exactly half their vertices under a natural index-two symmetry constraint. The theorem identifies a surprisingly universal and strongly parity-dependent angular width law, with exact all-rank zero-defect probability and a full order-of-n contrast between worst-case and typical metric loss. This goes beyond restating either single orbit-support formula and resolves natural cross-type geometric invariants for all generic orbit weights.
